label: 3rd input token after an opening pair drawn from {0, i}
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost always at t=2 (98% of mass), when the first two original tokens are both drawn from {0, i} (00, 0i, i0, ii). The token at t=2 can be anything. In the examples, magnitude is highest for the opening pair 0 0 (b at t=2 hits the max) and lowest for i i (about 0.25-0.3 of max), with 0 i and i 0 in between. A small weak tail fires at t=3 when the {0,i} pair sits at steps 1-2. It never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, and does not fire on a {0,i} pair that appears later in the sequence.

issues: The claims hold up on the test split. The predicate has precision 1.0 with 0 false positives and recall 0.888. The 291 missed steps carry only 2.3% of activation mass. 'phase!=0' scores 0 everywhere, so the feature never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase. The profile puts 98.4% of mass at t=2 and 1.6% at t=3.

The magnitude ordering checks out (test quartile coverage, lowest to highest quartile). 00 at t=2: [0, 0, 0.21, 0.69], so it holds the top activations. ii: [0.23, 0, 0.03, 0]. i0: [0.76, 0.07, 0.04, ...]. 0i: [0, 0.71, 0.24, ...]. So 00 > 0i > i0 > ii. Lumping 0i and i0 together as 'in between' is fine. Note that i0 sits closer to ii than 0i does.

The t=3 tail is overstated slightly. A {0,i} pair at steps 1-2 is necessary but not enough: the predicate (t==3)&pair at orig(1),orig(2) has precision only 0.086 (mass recall 0.019). The tail must depend on something else as well, such as orig(0) (misses show 'b 0 0', 'a 0 0', '1 0 0'). This is negligible in mass.

There is a minor extra miss class: t=2 with orig(1)=='0' but orig(0) not in {0,i} (e.g. 'a 0 b', 'm 0 b'). These fire weakly (about 0.07-0.11 of max) and are concentrated on in_tok b. The mass is too small to be systematic.
